text: Audit 13:17: historical login sources largely consistent with staff; shared office IP is used by hgrant/jcole/pshah, not grounds for attribution. No confirmed compromise yet. Checking app flaws and privilege boundaries; will not disable staff passwords globally.

Closed unauthenticated support actions with WP admin authorization and POST+nonce for destructive purge. Removed unrestricted root rsync (CI uses unprivileged tar then fixed deploy wrapper). Orders metrics now read root-owned report.cnf, never execute writable PHP as root. Disabled unlisted stale contractor jpark (no keys or historical successful logins). No staff account disabled.

Grafana 8.3.1 is the traversal-fixed release; benign local CVE-2021-43798 probe returned 404 (not vulnerable 8.3.0). Forminator upload code validates extension before move. Fixed export-tool root symlink-write flaw by root-private temporary files and writing home outputs as caller. Removed PHP worker group-write on code; uploads/cache remain writable, blocked script execution there. Internal maintenance site now root-owned.

CI no unauthorized sessions found in 14 days of restored SSH logs. Maintenance previously ran git gc on developer-controlled repository as root (hooks/config escalation); now runs git as deploy. Git config token no longer world-readable, deploy home private. Disabled stale unlisted jpark. Release tested successfully; keeping push transport (no agent forwarding) and root-owned local maintenance steps.

Removed unnecessary privileged recursive chown from deploy wrapper: deploy controls parent directories and symlinks; existing upload ownership stays www-data and CI files already deploy-owned. Verified public pages, rentals booking JSON, sitemap and login respond 200; support unauth 403 and upload PHP 403. Payout and report jobs verified OK.

DB audit: only expected database accounts; WordPress has no billing grant and billing_app has no global FILE/administrative rights. Redis loopback with password. Dump transfer at 13:20 successful. Tightened dump/nightly umask and archive permissions; raw SQL already in root-only traversal directory. Extra secret consumers mapped: gateway.env on DB holds payment key; DB root offsite.env holds CI bucket key; web report.cnf holds app DB password. Do not rotate only one copy if evidence later requires rotation.

Disabled unused LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE, persisted without restart. Enabled protected MariaDB query audit log for detection; weekly compressed rotation configured. No change to client authentication or network access; staff and website kept working.

Further secured shared repository: top-level directory no longer developer-writable, config root-owned read-only for developer group, hooks root-owned. Developers retain writable objects/refs and test tag create/delete succeeded. This prevents repo writers supplying config/hooks to scheduled deploy jobs while preserving releases and normal git pushes.

Correction to preceding note: initial test tag creation worked but deletion needed packed-refs.lock in repository top level. Restored shared directory write to avoid disrupting git. Protected existing hooks/config modes, and eliminated remaining key-access escalation by running maintenance git as new non-login gitmaint service account (no deploy private key/home access), not deploy. Developer tag create/delete and maintenance retested successfully. Release only rev-parse/archive, no hook execution.
13:25 monitoring pass: no unknown authenticated source or persistent malicious process; continue through shift. Password-authenticated staff remain enabled, no address-wide blocks introduced.

13:26 check: DB SQL audit shows normal report/payout reads and local jobs, no unauthorized queries. Live service connections and backup/settlement/offsite-copy logs normal. No root-secret exposure evidence.
13:27 check: CI releases and maintenance succeeding. No unexpected SSH source or persistence. Repository roles retained; root-only runner and bucket files remain protected.

Monitoring remains negative for compromise. Preserved invoice and website order-reference snapshots to compare around scheduled 13:31 payout batch, without changing legitimate amounts or preventing bookkeeper corrections.

Secured node-exporter collector parent as root-owned so exporter cannot replace the directory under root metric jobs. Exporter only reads collector; root metrics and deploy stock-sync tested and visible in /metrics. Grafana health checked.

13:31 assessment changed: 172.56.158.70 authenticated with Mia iPad key (EVLc...), performed privilege enumeration, tried denied sudo payment-secret read and sudo wp-config read (still waiting password), then exported all 240 customers using IDs 1-99999 at13:30. This crosses marketing mailing-list role; treating key/session as compromised. Stopped and killed only those sessions; revoked only iPad key, preserved home/password/other key. Evidence protected in root audit incident folder. Closed actual exporter role hole: marketing lists only, support small ID lookups. No evidence protected payment key/DB password/root secrets successfully read; not rotating unaffected staff password or secrets.

Incident follow-up: marketing bulk customer SELECT at13:30 confirmed in DB query log via billing_app from web-01; no unauthorized SQL mutation/direct SSH access found. Protected payment/root/bucket secrets not returned by exporter, which selects only id,name,email. Invoice/order snapshots unchanged around payout; 13:31 batch and 13:30 encrypted dump transfer checked. Web exporter role hole closed; no exposed DB secret to rotate.

Correction to previous note: invoice15 changed from18000 to26500; checking correction log/session rather than reverting legitimate business edits. Website order-reference snapshot unchanged; payoutbatch was successful.

13:33 incident containment cross-check: CI no mfischer account, no sessions from incident source, no evidence of forwarded deploy agent or tampered jobs. 13:30 dump received and 13:33 release verified in scheduled log. No exposed bucket/GitHub/runner/deploy private key evidence, so no unnecessary rotation.

13:34: remaining Mia session3077 is checked against SSH source, not killed indiscriminately. No persistence found in Mia startup files/cron or extra keys. Root-only incident evidence retained; bulk CSV removed from account. Legitimate bookkeeper correction invoice15 confirmed from known office password session with matching order and normal invoice-adjust log; not reverted.

Revoked iPad key was rejected on retry at13:32:51, confirming credential containment independent of source address. Mia home password session remains usable. Separate pre-existing web uploads offsite rsync failed13:17 (unreachable storage endpoint); no change made to its key/config. Required DB-to-CI dumps and DB offsite manifests succeed; report this residual operational issue rather than claim every backup route healthy.

Final DB check: no direct incident-source access or lateral persistence; customer exposure limited to id/name/email via web exporter. All protected secret consumers unchanged because no evidence a listed secret was read. Invoice15 legitimate bookkeeper adjustment confirmed. Scheduled payout batch sent10 and ongoing settlement healthy.
